item.text:
{
  "schema_version": "formalization-faithfulness-1",
  "role": "blind-translation",
  "dossier_sha256": "4e7e2daa30c8e9295f4576d64a68cd37bd0126e46a0b695fdbd83e2a984fea31",
  "dependency_coverage": [
    {
      "id": "D001",
      "name": "LocalDef001",
      "meaning": "At (x,t), there exist vectors qt and qx that are respectively the derivatives of τ ↦ q(x,τ) at t and ξ ↦ q(ξ,t) at x, and qt + A qx = 0.",
      "effect_on_target": "The vector PDE includes existence of both partial derivatives, not just a formal equation between derivative operators.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D002",
      "name": "LocalDef002",
      "meaning": "For a function taking values in a real normed vector space, both partial derivatives exist at (x,t), with values qt and qx satisfying qt + speed · qx = 0.",
      "effect_on_target": "Applied with scalar codomain Real, this expresses the scalar transport equation for each basis coordinate, including partial derivative existence.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D003",
      "name": "LocalDef003",
      "meaning": "There exist real eigenvalues indexed by the finite index type and a real basis of its real coordinate space such that each basis vector is an eigenvector with the corresponding eigenvalue.",
      "effect_on_target": "The hypothesis is diagonalizability over the reals. It does not require distinct eigenvalues, symmetry, or an orthonormal basis.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D004",
      "name": "LocalDef004",
      "meaning": "Real scalar multiplication on the space of real-valued functions on any index type is jointly continuous.",
      "effect_on_target": "Supplies continuity of scalar multiplication needed for the vector-valued partial derivative predicates.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D005",
      "name": "LocalDef005",
      "meaning": "Scalar multiplication is jointly continuous in every real normed vector space.",
      "effect_on_target": "Supplies the continuity structure needed in LocalDef002; it is not an additional assumption on q.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D006",
      "name": "Algebra.id",
      "meaning": "A commutative semiring is an algebra over itself with identity algebra map and scalar action given by multiplication.",
      "effect_on_target": "Real scalars acting on real coordinates use ordinary real multiplication.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D007",
      "name": "Algebra.toSMul",
      "meaning": "Extracts the scalar action from an algebra structure.",
      "effect_on_target": "Selects the usual real scalar action underlying vector scaling.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D008",
      "name": "And",
      "meaning": "Logical conjunction: both propositions hold.",
      "effect_on_target": "All three main properties hold for the same witnesses; both characteristic formulas hold under their shared hypotheses.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D009",
      "name": "CommSemiring.toSemiring",
      "meaning": "Retains the semiring structure of a commutative semiring.",
      "effect_on_target": "Provides the ordinary real semiring operations for algebra and module constructions.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D010",
      "name": "DFinsupp.instEquivLikeLinearEquiv",
      "meaning": "Provides the equivalence-like interface for a linear equivalence, including its underlying bijection.",
      "effect_on_target": "Allows the basis coordinate equivalence to be applied to q(x,t).",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D011",
      "name": "DFunLike.coe",
      "meaning": "Extracts the underlying function from a function-like object.",
      "effect_on_target": "Interprets b(i) as a basis vector and b.equivFun(v)(i) as a scalar coordinate.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D012",
      "name": "DenselyNormedField.toNontriviallyNormedField",
      "meaning": "A densely normed field has a nontrivial normed-field structure with the same field and norm.",
      "effect_on_target": "Supplies the real scalar-field structure required for differentiability.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D013",
      "name": "Differentiable",
      "meaning": "The function is differentiable at every point of its domain.",
      "effect_on_target": "The characteristic formulas require joint real differentiability of (x,t) ↦ q(x,t) everywhere on R²; continuity of its derivative is not required.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D014",
      "name": "DivisionSemiring.toSemiring",
      "meaning": "Extracts the underlying semiring from a division semiring.",
      "effect_on_target": "Supplies unchanged real arithmetic in the module structures used by differentiability.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D015",
      "name": "Eq",
      "meaning": "Equality of two objects of the same type.",
      "effect_on_target": "All eigenvector, PDE, coordinate, and reconstruction equalities are exact; vector equality means equality at every coordinate.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D016",
      "name": "EquivLike.toFunLike",
      "meaning": "Views an equivalence-like object as a function-like object using its forward map.",
      "effect_on_target": "The coordinate expressions use the forward basis coordinate map.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D017",
      "name": "Exists",
      "meaning": "Existential quantification over a witness satisfying the stated predicate.",
      "effect_on_target": "One speed family and one basis are chosen before q, x, and t; derivative witnesses in the PDE predicates are local to each function and point.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D018",
      "name": "Field.toSemifield",
      "meaning": "Retains the semifield operations and laws of a field.",
      "effect_on_target": "Provides a structural path to the standard real semiring used for differentiation.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D019",
      "name": "Fin",
      "meaning": "Fin m is the type of natural-number indices i with 0 ≤ i < m.",
      "effect_on_target": "Vectors, basis vectors, speeds, and matrix rows and columns have exactly m indices; m may be zero.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D020",
      "name": "Fin.fintype",
      "meaning": "Enumerates all indices in Fin n using the finite range of length n.",
      "effect_on_target": "Makes matrix products and reconstruction sums finite sums over all m indices.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D021",
      "name": "Finite.of_fintype",
      "meaning": "An explicitly finitely enumerated type is finite.",
      "effect_on_target": "Enables the full function-valued coordinate equivalence for the finite basis index set.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D022",
      "name": "Finset.sum",
      "meaning": "Adds the values of a function over a finite set in an additive commutative monoid.",
      "effect_on_target": "Reconstructs q as a finite vector sum, with the empty sum equal to the zero vector.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D023",
      "name": "Finset.univ",
      "meaning": "The finite set containing every element of a finitely enumerated type.",
      "effect_on_target": "The reconstruction includes every basis index exactly once.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D024",
      "name": "Function.hasSMul",
      "meaning": "Lifts scalar multiplication on a codomain to pointwise scalar multiplication on functions.",
      "effect_on_target": "Multiplying a vector by a speed or coefficient scales each real coordinate.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D025",
      "name": "Function.uncurry",
      "meaning": "Transforms q into the function (x,t) ↦ q(x)(t) on ordered pairs.",
      "effect_on_target": "The regularity assumption concerns joint differentiability in space and time.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D026",
      "name": "HMul.hMul",
      "meaning": "Extracts the multiplication operation from its instance.",
      "effect_on_target": "The characteristic displacement contains the real product speeds(i) · t.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D027",
      "name": "HSMul.hSMul",
      "meaning": "Extracts a scalar multiplication operation.",
      "effect_on_target": "Expresses real scaling of eigenvectors and reconstructed basis terms, and scalar multiplication in the transport equation.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D028",
      "name": "HSub.hSub",
      "meaning": "Extracts the subtraction operation.",
      "effect_on_target": "The initial spatial argument is x minus speeds(i) times t.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D029",
      "name": "Iff",
      "meaning": "Logical equivalence, asserting implication in both directions.",
      "effect_on_target": "At each point, the vector PDE holds exactly when every scalar coordinate PDE holds.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D030",
      "name": "LinearEquiv",
      "meaning": "An invertible semilinear map, with scalar maps specified by mutually inverse ring homomorphisms.",
      "effect_on_target": "Here both scalar maps are the identity on R, so the coordinate map is an ordinary real-linear bijection.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D031",
      "name": "Matrix",
      "meaning": "A matrix is a function from a row index and a column index to an entry.",
      "effect_on_target": "A is an arbitrary fixed m-by-m array of real entries subject to the real eigenbasis hypothesis.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D032",
      "name": "Matrix.mulVec",
      "meaning": "For a matrix A and vector v, the row-j coordinate of A v is the dot product of row j with v, namely the sum of A(j,k)v(k) over k.",
      "effect_on_target": "Fixes left matrix action on column vectors in the eigenvector equations and in ∂t q + A ∂x q = 0.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D033",
      "name": "Module.Basis",
      "meaning": "An indexed algebraic basis of a module, providing unique finitely supported scalar coordinates.",
      "effect_on_target": "b is a linearly independent spanning family of m vectors in R^m, not merely a collection of eigenvectors.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D034",
      "name": "Module.Basis.equivFun",
      "meaning": "For a finite basis index set, sends a vector to its basis representation viewed as an ordinary coordinate function.",
      "effect_on_target": "b.equivFun(q(x,t))(i) is the coefficient of b(i) in q(x,t), not necessarily its i-th standard coordinate.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D035",
      "name": "Module.Basis.instFunLike",
      "meaning": "The i-th basis vector is the inverse representation image of the coefficient function supported at i with value one.",
      "effect_on_target": "The eigenvector and reconstruction expressions refer to the basis vectors associated with the same coordinate map.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D036",
      "name": "Nat",
      "meaning": "The natural numbers, including zero.",
      "effect_on_target": "The dimension m is universally quantified without a positivity requirement.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D037",
      "name": "Ne",
      "meaning": "Negation of equality.",
      "effect_on_target": "Each indexed basis vector is explicitly asserted to differ from the zero vector.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D038",
      "name": "NonAssocSemiring.toNonUnitalNonAssocSemiring",
      "meaning": "Forgets the designated unit while retaining addition and multiplication.",
      "effect_on_target": "Provides unchanged real operations to algebraic infrastructure.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D039",
      "name": "NonUnitalCommRing.toNonUnitalNonAssocCommRing",
      "meaning": "Retains a nonunital commutative ring's operations while dropping the associativity requirement from the interface.",
      "effect_on_target": "Part of the structural route supplying real arithmetic for matrix multiplication.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D040",
      "name": "NonUnitalNonAssocCommRing.toNonUnitalNonAssocRing",
      "meaning": "Forgets multiplication commutativity while preserving the underlying ring operations.",
      "effect_on_target": "Does not alter the real operations used in A.mulVec.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D041",
      "name": "NonUnitalNonAssocRing.toNonUnitalNonAssocSemiring",
      "meaning": "Retains addition, zero, multiplication, and distributive laws without requiring additive inverses in the resulting interface.",
      "effect_on_target": "Supplies the algebraic structure required by matrix-vector multiplication.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D042",
      "name": "NonUnitalNonAssocSemiring.toAddCommMonoid",
      "meaning": "Extracts the additive commutative monoid of a semiring-like structure.",
      "effect_on_target": "Coordinates and coordinate functions use ordinary additive structure.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D043",
      "name": "NonUnitalNormedCommRing.toNonUnitalCommRing",
      "meaning": "Forgets norm data and retains the nonunital commutative ring operations.",
      "effect_on_target": "Links the standard real normed structure to the arithmetic used by A.mulVec.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D044",
      "name": "NonUnitalSeminormedCommRing.toNonUnitalSeminormedRing",
      "meaning": "Forgets multiplication commutativity from a nonunital seminormed commutative ring.",
      "effect_on_target": "Preserves the real norm and operations used to obtain the scalar normed additive structure.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D045",
      "name": "NonUnitalSeminormedRing.toSeminormedAddCommGroup",
      "meaning": "Extracts the additive group, norm, and associated pseudometric from a seminormed ring.",
      "effect_on_target": "Provides the real seminormed additive structure underlying real normed vector spaces.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D046",
      "name": "NonUnitalSemiring.toNonUnitalNonAssocSemiring",
      "meaning": "Drops the associativity requirement from the interface while retaining operations.",
      "effect_on_target": "Provides unchanged real addition and multiplication for module infrastructure.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D047",
      "name": "NontriviallyNormedField.toNormedField",
      "meaning": "Extracts the underlying normed field.",
      "effect_on_target": "Differentiation and module operations use the same real normed field.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D048",
      "name": "NormedCommRing.toNonUnitalNormedCommRing",
      "meaning": "Retains a normed commutative ring's norm, metric, and ring operations while forgetting its designated unit.",
      "effect_on_target": "Does not change real arithmetic or topology in the matrix expressions.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D049",
      "name": "NormedCommRing.toSeminormedCommRing",
      "meaning": "Views a normed commutative ring as seminormed with the same norm and operations.",
      "effect_on_target": "Preserves the standard real norm used in the module structure.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D050",
      "name": "NormedField.toField",
      "meaning": "Extracts the field structure from a normed field.",
      "effect_on_target": "The real arithmetic underlying differentiability is unchanged.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D051",
      "name": "NormedField.toNormedSpace",
      "meaning": "A normed field is a normed vector space over itself with scalar action given by multiplication.",
      "effect_on_target": "The scalar transport functions take values in the standard real normed vector space.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D052",
      "name": "NormedSpace.toModule",
      "meaning": "Extracts the module structure from a normed vector space.",
      "effect_on_target": "Basis and differentiability constructions use the same real scalar action.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D053",
      "name": "OfNat.ofNat",
      "meaning": "Interprets a natural-number literal using the specified instance.",
      "effect_on_target": "The displayed zero literals denote either real zero or the zero vector according to their types.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D054",
      "name": "Pi.Function.module",
      "meaning": "Functions into a module form a module under pointwise operations.",
      "effect_on_target": "Fin m → Real is the usual real vector space R^m.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D055",
      "name": "Pi.addCommGroup",
      "meaning": "Functions into additive commutative groups form an additive commutative group pointwise.",
      "effect_on_target": "Vector addition, subtraction, and negation are coordinatewise.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D056",
      "name": "Pi.addCommMonoid",
      "meaning": "Functions into additive commutative monoids form an additive commutative monoid pointwise.",
      "effect_on_target": "The reconstruction sum is a coordinatewise vector sum.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D057",
      "name": "Pi.instZero",
      "meaning": "The zero function assigns zero to every index.",
      "effect_on_target": "The excluded zero eigenvector and the PDE zero vector have every component zero.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D058",
      "name": "Pi.topologicalSpace",
      "meaning": "The function space carries the product topology induced by all coordinate evaluations.",
      "effect_on_target": "The finite-dimensional target R^m has its usual topology for differentiability and vector derivatives.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D059",
      "name": "Prod",
      "meaning": "The Cartesian product type of ordered pairs.",
      "effect_on_target": "The jointly differentiated domain consists of pairs (x,t) in R².",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D060",
      "name": "Prod.instAddCommGroup",
      "meaning": "The Cartesian product of additive commutative groups has componentwise group operations.",
      "effect_on_target": "The space-time domain has ordinary vector addition on R².",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D061",
      "name": "Prod.instModule",
      "meaning": "The product of two modules is a module under componentwise scalar multiplication.",
      "effect_on_target": "Joint differentiation uses the usual real vector-space structure on R².",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D062",
      "name": "PseudoMetricSpace.toUniformSpace",
      "meaning": "Extracts the uniform structure associated with a pseudometric.",
      "effect_on_target": "Connects the real absolute-value metric to the topology used in differentiation.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D063",
      "name": "Real",
      "meaning": "The real number type.",
      "effect_on_target": "Matrix entries, speeds, coordinates, space, and time are all real.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D064",
      "name": "Real.denselyNormedField",
      "meaning": "The standard real normed field has norms attaining values between any two positive real bounds.",
      "effect_on_target": "Supplies the nontrivial norm required for real differentiation; adds no hypothesis on q or A.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D065",
      "name": "Real.instAddCommGroup",
      "meaning": "The additive commutative group structure of the reals.",
      "effect_on_target": "Provides real addition and additive inverses for the domain and codomain.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D066",
      "name": "Real.instAddCommMonoid",
      "meaning": "The additive commutative monoid structure of the reals.",
      "effect_on_target": "Supports vector-space and finite-sum constructions with ordinary real addition.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D067",
      "name": "Real.instCommSemiring",
      "meaning": "The commutative semiring structure of the reals.",
      "effect_on_target": "Supports the identity real algebra and ordinary scalar multiplication.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D068",
      "name": "Real.instMul",
      "meaning": "Real multiplication.",
      "effect_on_target": "Determines the displacement speeds(i) times t.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D069",
      "name": "Real.instRing",
      "meaning": "The ring structure of the reals.",
      "effect_on_target": "Provides the standard arithmetic for the real module used in differentiability.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D070",
      "name": "Real.instSub",
      "meaning": "Real subtraction, defined as addition of the additive inverse.",
      "effect_on_target": "Determines the sign in the characteristic foot x − speeds(i)t.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D071",
      "name": "Real.instZero",
      "meaning": "The real number zero.",
      "effect_on_target": "The formulas evaluate q at time zero and use real zero in the scalar PDE.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D072",
      "name": "Real.normedAddCommGroup",
      "meaning": "The real additive group with its standard absolute-value norm and metric.",
      "effect_on_target": "Scalar partial derivatives use the usual real topology.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D073",
      "name": "Real.normedCommRing",
      "meaning": "The usual real commutative ring equipped with its standard norm and metric.",
      "effect_on_target": "Ensures algebraic and analytic structures in the target use ordinary real operations.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D074",
      "name": "Real.normedField",
      "meaning": "The real field with its standard norm and metric.",
      "effect_on_target": "Provides the scalar field for all derivatives and normed vector spaces.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D075",
      "name": "Real.pseudoMetricSpace",
      "meaning": "The real distance is |x − y|, with its associated uniform structure.",
      "effect_on_target": "Fixes the usual topology on space, time, and real coordinates.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D076",
      "name": "Real.semiring",
      "meaning": "The standard semiring structure of the reals.",
      "effect_on_target": "Provides ordinary real addition and multiplication in the basis and coordinate modules.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D077",
      "name": "Ring.toSemiring",
      "meaning": "Retains a ring's semiring structure.",
      "effect_on_target": "No arithmetic change occurs when the real ring is used by module infrastructure.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D078",
      "name": "RingHom.id",
      "meaning": "The identity ring homomorphism r ↦ r.",
      "effect_on_target": "The basis coordinate equivalence preserves real scalars without any scalar twist.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D079",
      "name": "RingHomInvPair.ids",
      "meaning": "The identity ring homomorphism is inverse to itself.",
      "effect_on_target": "Supports the ordinary real-linear equivalence type of the coordinate map.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D080",
      "name": "Semifield.toDivisionSemiring",
      "meaning": "Retains division-semiring structure and operations from a semifield.",
      "effect_on_target": "Supplies unchanged real arithmetic through a structural conversion.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D081",
      "name": "SeminormedCommRing.toNonUnitalSeminormedCommRing",
      "meaning": "Forgets the designated unit while preserving seminorm, pseudometric, and ring operations.",
      "effect_on_target": "Preserves the scalar norm and additive structure used by real normed spaces.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D082",
      "name": "Semiring.toModule",
      "meaning": "A semiring acts as a module over itself by multiplication.",
      "effect_on_target": "Real coefficients act on real coordinates by ordinary multiplication.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D083",
      "name": "Semiring.toNonAssocSemiring",
      "meaning": "Retains semiring operations while omitting the associativity requirement from the interface.",
      "effect_on_target": "Supports identity ring homomorphisms and additive structures without changing real operations.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D084",
      "name": "Semiring.toNonUnitalSemiring",
      "meaning": "Retains semiring operations while forgetting the designated unit.",
      "effect_on_target": "Provides a structural route to the real additive monoid used in differentiation.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D085",
      "name": "UniformSpace.toTopologicalSpace",
      "meaning": "Extracts the topology belonging to a uniform space.",
      "effect_on_target": "The real and product topologies used in derivative predicates come from the standard metric.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D086",
      "name": "Zero.toOfNat0",
      "meaning": "Interprets the numeral 0 as the zero of the given type.",
      "effect_on_target": "Zero literals are the real zero or coordinatewise vector zero.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D087",
      "name": "instHMul",
      "meaning": "Uses ordinary multiplication as the heterogeneous multiplication operation on one type.",
      "effect_on_target": "The speed-time product is ordinary real multiplication.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D088",
      "name": "instHSMul",
      "meaning": "Uses a scalar action as the heterogeneous scalar multiplication operation.",
      "effect_on_target": "The displayed scalar products use the selected usual real scalar actions.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D089",
      "name": "instHSub",
      "meaning": "Uses ordinary subtraction as the heterogeneous subtraction operation on one type.",
      "effect_on_target": "The spatial shift is ordinary real subtraction.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {

  "translation": {
    "binders": [
      "For every natural number m, including m = 0, let I = {0,...,m−1} and V = R^I.",
      "For every real matrix A indexed by I × I satisfying the stated real eigenbasis hypothesis, there exist a function λ : I → R, corresponding to speeds, and a real basis b = (b_i)_{i∈I} of V.",
      "The same λ and b are chosen before all subsequent universal quantifiers and work simultaneously for every q : R → R → V and all real x and t.",
      "In the pointwise PDE equivalence, q, x, and t are arbitrary, and the scalar equations are quantified over every i ∈ I.",
      "In the characteristic conclusion, q is universally quantified subject to joint differentiability and the vector PDE everywhere; the coordinate identity is universal in i, x, and t, and reconstruction is universal in x and t.",
      "Within each local PDE predicate, the derivative witnesses qt and qx are existentially quantified and may depend on the function, coefficient or speed, and point; scalar witnesses also depend on i."
    ],
    "hypotheses": [
      "A has a real eigenbasis: there exist μ : I → R and a real basis e of V such that A e_i = μ_i e_i for every i ∈ I.",
      "For the characteristic and reconstruction conclusions only, Q : R² → V, Q(x,t) = q(x,t), is real differentiable at every point.",
      "For those same conclusions, q satisfies the vector PDE at every real (x,t): both partial derivatives exist and ∂t q(x,t) + A ∂x q(x,t) = 0."
    ],
    "conclusions": [
      "There exist λ : I → R and a real basis b of V satisfying all following properties together.",
      "For every i ∈ I, b_i ≠ 0 and A b_i = λ_i b_i.",
      "Write c_b(v)_i for the coefficient of b_i in v, and u_i(x,t) = c_b(q(x,t))_i. For every q and every real (x,t), existence of the two vector partial derivatives with ∂t q(x,t) + A ∂x q(x,t) = 0 is equivalent to the assertion that, for every i ∈ I, both partial derivatives of u_i exist there and ∂t u_i(x,t) + λ_i ∂x u_i(x,t) = 0.",
      "For every jointly differentiable q satisfying the vector PDE everywhere, u_i(x,t) = u_i(x − λ_i t,0) for every i ∈ I and every real x,t.",
      "For the same q, q(x,t) = Σ_{i∈I} c_b(q(x − λ_i t,0))_i b_i for every real x,t."
    ],
    "mathematical_definitions": [
      "V = R^I has coordinatewise addition and real scalar multiplication and its usual finite product topology.",
      "Matrix action is (A v)_j = Σ_{k∈I} A_{jk} v_k.",
      "A basis is a linearly independent spanning family; its coordinate map c_b is the real-linear bijection characterized by v = Σ_{i∈I} c_b(v)_i b_i.",
      "The vector PDE at (x,t) means that there exist qt,qx ∈ V with d/dτ q(x,τ)|_{τ=t} = qt and d/dξ q(ξ,t)|_{ξ=x} = qx, and qt + A qx = 0.",
      "The scalar transport PDE at speed λ_i means that there exist a,d ∈ R with d/dτ u_i(x,τ)|_{τ=t} = a and d/dξ u_i(ξ,t)|_{ξ=x} = d, and a + λ_i d = 0.",
      "All slice derivatives are ordinary derivatives on the whole real line. Joint differentiability refers to differentiability of Q on R², not merely separate differentiability.",
      "The constant 0 in q(x − λ_i t,0) is the initial time; the minus sign specifies translation by λ_i t from that initial profile."
    ],
    "proposition_plain_english": "Every finite real square matrix possessing a real eigenbasis admits a choice of real speeds λ_i and a basis b_i of nonzero eigenvectors such that the constant-coefficient system ∂t q + A ∂x q = 0 is pointwise equivalent, for every function q, to the scalar equations ∂t u_i + λ_i ∂x u_i = 0 for its coordinates u_i in that basis. Both sides of this equivalence include existence of the relevant partial derivatives. With this same choice of speeds and basis, every everywhere jointly differentiable solution on all of R² has each coordinate transported from time zero according to u_i(x,t) = u_i(x − λ_i t,0), and its vector value is the sum of these transported initial coordinates multiplied by their respective basis vectors."
  },
  "restrictions_and_vacuity_risks": [
    "The matrix is finite-dimensional, real, square, and constant in x and t. The claim is conditional on diagonalizability over R, not merely on real eigenvalues.",
    "There is no positivity assumption on m. When m = 0, the index set is empty, V has only the zero vector, indexed assertions are vacuous, and reconstruction is the empty sum.",
    "For matrices without a real eigenbasis, the implication supplies no conclusion.",
    "Eigenvalues may repeat or be zero or negative. The basis need not be orthogonal or normalized, and its vectors need not have every standard coordinate nonzero.",
    "The pointwise PDE equivalence has no independent continuity or joint differentiability assumption on q. Its two sides themselves assert existence of the relevant slice derivatives.",
    "The characteristic formulas apply only to everywhere jointly differentiable solutions on the whole plane. Separate differentiability alone is not the stated hypothesis, and continuous differentiability is not required.",
    "Space and time range over all real numbers, including negative time. No boundary, restricted spatial domain, or finite time interval is encoded.",
    "The formulas use the existing solution's trace at time zero. There is no separately quantified prescribed initial datum and no explicit assertion that arbitrary initial data generate a differentiable solution.",
    "The reconstruction determines any solution in the stated class from its time-zero trace, but the target does not separately quantify a uniqueness theorem comparing two solutions.",
    "No weak, distributional, discontinuous-solution, stability, or continuous-dependence statement is encoded.",
    "The speed family and basis are common to all functions and points; they are existential choices, not asserted to be canonical or unique.",
    "For a q failing either global hypothesis of the characteristic implication, that implication gives no characteristic or reconstruction constraint. Constant functions do satisfy the hypotheses, so the solution class is not intrinsically empty."
  ],
  "ambiguities": []
